chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the Imam: has Allah delegated to him just as He delegated to Sulayman ibn Dawud? He said: Yes. And that is that a man asked him about an issue, so he answered him concerning it; then another asked him about that same issue, so he answered him differently from the answer given to the first; then another asked him, and he answered him differently from the answer given to the first two. Then he said:
"This is Our gift, so withhold or give without reckoning."
And this is how it is in the recitation of Ali عليه السلام.
I said: May Allah keep you well, so when he answers them with this answer, does the Imam recognize them? He said: Glory be to Allah! Do you not hear Allah saying:
"Surely in that are signs for those who discern."
"And indeed it is on an abiding road."

Then he said to me: Yes, when the Imam looks at a man, he recognizes him and recognizes his color; and if he hears his speech from behind a wall, he recognizes him and recognizes what he is. Indeed Allah says:
"And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your tongues and your colors. Surely in that are signs for the knowing ones."

And they are the scholars. So he does not hear anything of a matter that is spoken except that he recognizes it, whether one saved or one doomed. Therefore, for that reason, he answers them with what he answers them.

key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: the Imams identified here as those possessing such discernment
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the divinely appointed Imam being discussed as possessing delegated authority
key_terms.الْعَالِمِينَ: the knowing ones, interpreted here as those endowed with true knowledge
key_terms.الْعُلَمَاءُ: the scholars, here referring to those possessing divinely granted recognition
key_terms.الْمُتَوَسِّمِينَ: those who discern signs and marks with insight
key_terms.فَوَّضَ: delegated or entrusted with authority by Allah
key_terms.مَسْأَلَةٍ: a question or legal/religious issue brought for answer

ai.seo_question: How does the Imam know people’s inner condition and why may he answer the same question differently?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a divinely granted authority and discernment given to the Imam, likened to what was granted to Sulayman ibn Dawud. It explains that the Imam may answer similar questions differently because he knows the inner state and condition of the questioners. It also connects this discernment to Qur'anic verses about signs for those who truly perceive and know.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Idrees and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Ubeys Bin Hisham, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Imam<sup>asws</sup>.

‘Has Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Authorise to him<sup>asws</sup> just as He<sup>azwj</sup> had Authorised to Suleyman<sup>as</sup> Bin Dawood<sup>as</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. And that is, that a man asked him<sup>asws</sup> a question, so he<sup>asws</sup> answered him with regards to it; and another man asked him that very question, so he<sup>asws</sup> answered him with other than the answer of the first one. Then another one asked him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> answered him with other than the answer of the two former ones.
Then heasws said: ‘[38:39] This is Our Gift, therefore withhold or give out freely without measure; and like this it is in the recitation of Aliasws’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘May Allahazwj Keep youasws well! So when heasws answers them with these answers, does the Imamasws understand them?’ Heasws said: ‘Glory be to Allahazwj! Have you not hear Allahazwj Saying [15:75] Surely, in this are Signs for those who distinguish (the marks)?
And theyasws are the Imamsasws [15:76] And surely it is on a road that still abides, not coming out from it, ever!’

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Yes, the Imam<sup>asws</sup>, when he looks at the man, he<sup>asws</sup> recognises him<sup>asws</sup> and recognises his<sup>asws</sup> colour, and if he<sup>asws</sup> hears his<sup>asws</sup> speech from behind a wall, recognises him and recognises who is he.
Allahazwj is Saying [30:22] And from His Signs is the creation of the skies and the earth and the diversity of your tongues and colours; most surely there are Signs in this for the scholar.

And they<sup>asws</sup> are the Scholars. So there isn’t anything from the matters spoken with that he<sup>asws</sup> hears except that he<sup>asws</sup> would recognise it whether he is a saved one or a destroyed one. Therefore, due to that, he<sup>asws</sup> answers them by that which he<sup>asws</sup> answers them with’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya havenarrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kufi from ‘Ubays ibn Hisham from ‘Abdallah ibn Sulayman who has said the following.

“I asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the Imam. Has Allah made him the in charge of the and in full control (over the affairs of the people) as Sulayman ibn Dawud was?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Yes, he is given control. It is because a man asked him a question and he gave the answer. Another person asked the same question and he gave him a different answer (although the question was the same). A third person asked him the same question and he gave an answer that was different from both the previous answers. Then he said,
“This is Our gift to you so give them away free or keep them as you like.” [38:39]. This is charity from us enjoy it with thanks or ( give to others) without being questioned.
This is according to Imam Ali’s recitation.”

The narrator has said that I said to him, “May Allah grant you well being, when the he gives such answers does the Imam know them?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Glory belongs to Allah. Have you not heard Allah words?
“ In this there is evidence (of the Truth) for the discreet ones. [15:75]
That town lies on a road which still exists [15:76]
Then The Imam (a.s.) said to me, “Yes, when the Imam look at a person he recognizes him and his color. On hearing his words even from behind the wall he recognizes him and what he is. Allah has said,
“Other evidence of His existence are the creation of the heavens and the earth and the differences of languages and colors. In this there is evidence (of the truth) for the worlds (mankind).” [30:22]

The Imams are the scholars. Whatever they would hear that is spoken they recognize it, the one who has received salvation or one who is destroyed. For this reason they answer them as they answer them.”
